set.explanation: Every assessed pair is consistent under the stated rules.

rules.classification: Spectroscopic classes and alert or messenger labels are different definitions and are not compared; two active classes differ when neither label refines the other (for example 'SN Ia' and 'SN Ia-91T' agree); an earlier value from the same provider is a revision.
rules.host: Two proposed hosts agree when their names match after case and spacing are ignored or one name is among the other's NED cross-identifications; otherwise they are an identity ambiguity. Association probabilities are not computed.
rules.photometry: Only exactly compatible photometry (same epoch, band, system, method, calibration and direct/difference state, two or more providers) is compared. The limiting magnitude or flux that a provider reports alongside a detection is that epoch's detection threshold, not a non-detection, and is not compared with the detection; a detection brighter than another provider's non-detection limit at the same epoch is a status conflict. A group is listed only when it is still inconsistent under these rules; at most 10 groups per event, most significant first.
rules.position: Two positions with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they are more than 2 arcsec apart; when one states an error radius, the separation is compared with 3 times that radius.
rules.redshift: Two redshifts with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they differ by more than 0.005 (about 1,500 km/s); transient and host redshifts are different definitions and are listed, not compared; host redshifts of differently named hosts are an identity ambiguity.
rules.revision: A retracted row, or a superseded row of the same provider whose value differs beyond the property's rule, is a revision or retraction; a revision within the rule is consistent; the earlier value stays visible.
rules.sigma: Two values that both state an uncertainty are inconsistent when they differ by more than 3 combined standard deviations (uncertainties added in quadrature; a stated position error radius is treated as one standard deviation).

reported_assertions.remarks: Rising for 40 days. Now ~20 days after peak. Current brightness r~18.8 mag. g-r ~ 0.2 mag. Faint host in LS (r~21.71).
The light curve is similar to a Type II SN, but the plateau is ~120 days long and counting. g-r~+1.0 mag. Current brightness r~19.9 mag. Host detected in LS: r~20.5, photo-z = 0.088 +- 0.034.
Rising for &gt;40 days. Now around peak. Current brightness r~19.3 mag. g-r~+0.2. Host detected in LS: compact, r~21.0, photo-z = 0.233 +- 0.128.
Rising for ~35 days. Around peak. Current brightness r~19.6 mag. g-r~0. No host in DESI Legacy Survey.
Rising for &gt;45 days. Current brightness r~19.1 mag. g-r~0. No host in Legacy Survey.

Rose for ~50 days. The light curve remained flat around peak for ~30 days and is now fading. Current brightness r~20.2 mag. g-r~0.3 with large errors. Offset from an r~19.9 galaxy (LS photo-z = 0.398+-0.052).
Rising for 30 days and since then on a plateau. Current brightness 20.3 mag. g-r~0.2 mag. Host in LS (r~18.5, photo-z=0.139 +- 0.021)
Gradually rising for 20 days. Now around maximum. Current brightness r~19.1 mag. g-r~0 mag. Host in LS(r~20.2, photo-z=0.075 +- 0.034).
Rising for &gt;20 days. Current brightness r~19.9 mag. g-r~+0.8 mag, but EBV~0.07 mag. Host is very blue -&gt; strong emission lines. Brightness r~21.5. LS photo-z unreliable.
Rising for ~20 days. Flat light curve for ~34 days. Current brightness r~20 mag. g-r~0.6 mag. No host in PanSTARRS catalogue.

persistedQueryReceipts.scope: The anonymous AVSpec search interface explicitly searches published observations. Only rows returned by that interface and anonymously downloadable from the matching official record identifier are eligible. AAVSO states that its hosted data may be used in publications when the current Data Usage Guidelines are followed.

AAVSO states that International Database observations are freely available to the community for research and publication subject to its current Data Usage Guidelines. The v2 JSON API requires token authentication for access; authentication is not treated as a grant of proprietary rights. Only exact target-name and bounded date results from the documented photometry endpoint are eligible.

Only public ADS bibliographic metadata is retained. CTAS does not download, mirror, or assert reuse rights for article full text; publisher and repository links retain their own access and reuse terms. Event association requires an exact retained transient name.

The adapter uses ESO's anonymous TAP service only and retains a reduced-product row only when obs_release_date is present and no later than the query time. ESO states that the proprietary period protects raw and derived data until release and distributes archive data under CC BY 4.0 with acknowledgment requirements. No product bytes are downloaded.
No partial, malformed, or public-state-ambiguous mission row was stored.
Only observation and product rows explicitly marked PUBLIC are retained. Product bytes remain provider-hosted; this system stores metadata and official download links only.

The anonymous public NED TAP service documents programmatic cone searches of the NED Object Directory and requests NED acknowledgment. CTAS retains bounded source-native rows and provenance only. NED states that high-volume automated access is best-effort, so this adapter is single-threaded, starts at most one request per second, and never queries proprietary or user-account holdings.

Rubin alert packets are world-public with no proprietary period, and Fink documents its LSST Science Portal and REST API as real-time, public services requiring no login. Coordinate and first-detection proximity are not proof of source identity.
No unvalidated, non-public, or ambiguous scientific record was stored.

WISeREP's official help states that private data require a personal API key for scripted access. CTAS sends no credentials, requests public=yes explicitly, and accepts only rows independently marked public=1 from the anonymous public export.

A zero result means ALeRCE holds no public ZTF alert object at this position in the window; it is not a forced-photometry nondetection. Public ZTF alert photometry served by the ALeRCE broker. Cite Förster et al. (2021), AJ 161, 242, and acknowledge ALeRCE and the Zwicky Transient Facility according to current provider guidance.
A zero result may reflect public-release latency or catalog non-detection; it is not a forced-photometry nondetection.

selections.reason: Chosen by ctas-headline.v1 (naming-authority); the source rows are unchanged.

set.explanation: Every assessed pair is consistent under the stated rules.

rules.classification: Spectroscopic classes and alert or messenger labels are different definitions and are not compared; two active classes differ when neither label refines the other (for example 'SN Ia' and 'SN Ia-91T' agree); an earlier value from the same provider is a revision.
rules.host: Two proposed hosts agree when their names match after case and spacing are ignored or one name is among the other's NED cross-identifications; otherwise they are an identity ambiguity. Association probabilities are not computed.
rules.photometry: Only exactly compatible photometry (same epoch, band, system, method, calibration and direct/difference state, two or more providers) is compared. The limiting magnitude or flux that a provider reports alongside a detection is that epoch's detection threshold, not a non-detection, and is not compared with the detection; a detection brighter than another provider's non-detection limit at the same epoch is a status conflict. A group is listed only when it is still inconsistent under these rules; at most 10 groups per event, most significant first.
rules.position: Two positions with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they are more than 2 arcsec apart; when one states an error radius, the separation is compared with 3 times that radius.
rules.redshift: Two redshifts with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they differ by more than 0.005 (about 1,500 km/s); transient and host redshifts are different definitions and are listed, not compared; host redshifts of differently named hosts are an identity ambiguity.
rules.revision: A retracted row, or a superseded row of the same provider whose value differs beyond the property's rule, is a revision or retraction; a revision within the rule is consistent; the earlier value stays visible.
rules.sigma: Two values that both state an uncertainty are inconsistent when they differ by more than 3 combined standard deviations (uncertainties added in quadrature; a stated position error radius is treated as one standard deviation).
